TraceAnalysis: The incident summary indicates multiple trace call timeouts involving mobservice1, with call times exceeding the normal upper limit by 20-63 ms. These anomalies occurred in short time windows (e.g., 00:00:01–00:00:02) and across trace IDs ranging from ee5b090406f82ecc to dc87d3bfc5e8e2f5. The root cause has been identified as mobservice2, leading to service reliability degradation.
MetricAnalysis: The production incident at 2021/07/05 00:13:31 was caused by severe CPU utilization anomalies within the mobservice2 microservice. Key evidence includes extreme spikes in docker_cpu_core_0_ticks, docker_cpu_core_1_ticks, and docker_cpu_kernel_ticks metrics, each exhibiting sigma values exceeding 6. Concurrently, the docker_cpu_total_pct and docker_cpu_user_norm_pct metrics experienced significant transient upward shifts, confirming intense and abnormal CPU activity on this service.
LogAnalysis: The incident at 2021/07/05 00:21 was triggered by a failure in mobservice2, causing cascading issues across dependent services. The user-service experienced a surge of NullPointerExceptions in UserAuthenticationHandler due to unhandled null responses from mobservice2. Concurrently, the payment-gateway logged ServiceUnavailableException errors when external payment processor communication failed as mobservice2 became unavailable. The order-processing service also reported TimeoutException while attempting to connect to the impaired mobservice2. This resulted in widespread authentication, payment, and order fulfillment disruptions.
RootCauseAnalysis: The root cause of the incident was identified as an internal service error within mobservice2. Evidence indicates the service process completed unexpectedly ("Finished"). Service mobservice2 has recovered and is operating normally.
